headline: Computational methods refine quality control across single-cell and bulk sequencing
label: Computational Sequencing Quality Control
summary: Recent preprints and publications introduce computational filters and workflows that address noise and confounding in single-cell and bulk sequencing data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational quality control and quantification in sequencing-based profiling, where analysis choices shape which signal is recovered. A benchmark of scRNA-seq doublet detection reports that detection performs best before ambient RNA correction, with CellBender as the exception, indicating that processing order itself confounds results. Entropy-based filtering of nuclei in scATAC-seq uses genome-wide accessibility complexity as a quality criterion. HyARQ provides a Snakemake workflow for allele-specific read counting and QC across RNA-seq, MOA-seq, ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq in F1 hybrids. OmniRE-seq pairs bulk and single-cell RNA editing analyses for quantification, differential testing and annotation. Experimental advances, including RAPPL-Seq for ribosome profiling of scarce samples and droplet-based single-cell methylome profiling, extend the modalities these analyses must address. A published forensic analysis of complex DNA mixtures addresses single-cell isolation and genotype data integration.
